core.errors.note: SP-46: one taxonomy over every network call (src/core/http.ts): no answer is network-error with the failure as cause, 429 rate_limited with retryAfterSeconds, 5xx server-error with status and wireCode, 404 not_found, any other refusal the server's code; the server's message kept. Every exported error class is a PolarisError; every product-scoped call follows the WIRE-CONTRACT-V4 section 5 redirect rule (src/core/redirect.ts: cross-origin hops lose Authorization and X-PKey-*, insecure-redirect, too-many-redirects); activation and registration results print with the device token redacted (test/errorTaxonomy.test.ts).

except.note: When @napi-rs/keyring cannot load (a single-executable build, no Secret Service) the token is in a 0600 file; supports() reports dependency (P1b-10).

core.store.note: KeyringStore by default (reads are keyring-first; state written atomically at 0600 in a 0700 directory, read without following symlinks); an Electron main process uses SafeStorageStore (@polaris-key/node/electron), whose status() reports keyring-unavailable when safeStorage cannot encrypt or falls back to basic_text, and keyring-error when the stored token no longer decrypts (SP-N11).

core.copy.note: copy.message/title/activation over src/copy.generated.ts (pnpm gen constants, from conformance/parity/copy.en.json): the error-code, gate and activation tables, COPY_FALLBACK naming an unknown code; registerCopy adds a locale that falls back to the generated English per key.

core.backend.note: client.backend (packages/sdk-node/src/backend/client.ts): fetch() and headers() send X-PKey-License and X-PKey-Device only; backend.origins (exact, HTTPS except loopback) is checked on every hop, so a redirect cannot carry the licence elsewhere; the freshness pre-sync, one shared concurrent sync, one retry on license_stale/license_invalid, and not_entitled/sign_in_required thrown typed. Bridge v4 host verb core.backendHeaders. test/backend.test.ts replays backend-matrix.json's client rows.

core.devicekeys.note: createNodeDeviceKeyStore (src/devices/deviceKeys.ts) over node:crypto: a 0600 file in a 0700 state directory, cross-process lock file, atomic replace; an unreadable record is an error that only wipe() resets; PolarisKeyClient.devices.registerKeys sends PUT /devices/keys. On Windows the owner and mode checks, O_NOFOLLOW and the directory fsync are skipped (the profile ACL applies) and renames are retried on EPERM/EBUSY; stale-lock reclaim is best effort on a network home. The pkey-proof/1 signer is client-core's.

The connect-identity transcript replay is owed: no such transcript is recorded yet.

connect.noise.note: client-core's peer/noise.ts (NoiseHandshake, CipherState, peerPsk) over WebCrypto X25519 and AES-256-GCM, which the Node SDK consumes directly; the Node runner drives every noise-vectors.json row, the failures and the anchors (CC-05.2). The XXpsk0 anchor and the session machine follow.

connect.protocol.note: client-core's peer/ codecs (advert, sas, frame, record, relay, payload) and the PeerChannel session machine for modes a, v and p, which the Node SDK consumes directly; the Node runner drives every peer-matrix.json section (CC-05.4). The LAN sockets (connect.lan), the relay client (connect.relay) and the cloudConnect API (connect.app) are built on it.

connect.lan.note: client.connect.lan() (packages/sdk-node/src/connect, CC-08.2): LanService listens on TCP (one random port on a dual-stack `::` socket, falling back to 0.0.0.0; bounded unauthenticated sockets, per address and per /64, a handshake deadline, frames over 16 KiB refused before the handshake), advertises the account instance name on the epoch timer through an MdnsAdapter (multicast-dns 7.2.5, optional, behind an interface; adverts that do not verify against the roster, K_disc and two epochs are dropped; non-LAN addresses are never dialled) and dials with client-core's PeerChannel (Noise XXpsk0, certificate and roster admission, HELLO, MORE reassembly to 1 MiB, rekey). The device's X25519 key stays behind DeviceKeyPort.dh. ConnectSession gives send, receive, onMessage, onClose and close with typed LanError reasons. IPv6 (CC-IPV6.3, WIRE-CONTRACT-V5 §15.4 and §15.4.1): mDNS runs on 224.0.0.251 and on ff02::fb with one udp6 socket per interface (at most 8; the zone is the interface), with AAAA adverts and queries; a response from outside the receiving interface's connected subnets is ignored; an A or AAAA record is learned only when equal to the packet source (the mdnsAnswers rows run in test/mdnsAnswers.test.ts), at most 4 addresses per name; a peer is dialled in an RFC 8305 race (250 ms, 2 in flight) and every address is judged by client-core's lanVerdict as text before a socket exists and on the connected socket (and on an accepted one, before it is read) before the first byte. test/lan.e2e.test.ts, test/connectMdns.test.ts, test/mdnsAnswers.test.ts and test/connectHardening.test.ts (@pkey-feature connect.lan).

connect.relay.note: client.connect.relay() / client.cloudConnect (packages/sdk-node/src/connect/relay.ts, CC-08.3): connect.relayTicket() trades the bearer for a single-use pkeyrt_ ticket (shape-checked, wss and the Worker's own host only; typed RelayError for relay_disabled, relay_paused with Retry-After, relay_quota_exceeded with its scope); RelayService opens the WebSocket with pkey-relay.1 and the ticket, frames SEND, RECV, LIST, MEMBERS, RING, PING and LIMIT with client-core's envelope codec, runs one PeerChannel per (peer, session) in mode a only with the LAN's admission, reconnects with exponential backoff and jitter on a fresh ticket each time, and stops with a typed error on a spent quota, a disabled relay or a replaced socket (4009). Modes v and p never cross it (assertRelayMode; tested). A relay RING op above the held epoch, or a peer on a newer roster, fetches identity({refresh:true}); a pushed RING is stored under the identity fetch's rules and a pushed TRUST is verified and applied or refused with a reason. test/relay.test.ts (@pkey-feature connect.relay) runs against an in-process room with the CC-07 engine's framing; the connect-relay-ticket and connect-relay-quota transcripts replay in the Node runner.

connect.app.note: client.cloudConnect (packages/sdk-node/src/connect/cloudConnect.ts, CC-08.3): start({lan, relay, lanAttemptMs}), stop(), peers() with the paths each device has, refreshPeers(), devices(), open(deviceId) (LAN first, the relay after a failed or timed-out LAN attempt unless the host disabled it; session.path says which was used), onChannel(), onNotice() and status(). A LAN service that cannot start is not fatal while the relay is on. test/relay.test.ts (@pkey-feature connect.app). Nearby (mode v) and links (mode p) are later work packages.
